ledger.claim: The artifacts describe one and the same trip, and on this trip's own trace a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00115, and the trace's first fix at 21:10:00 matches the recorded start of the trip. Measured from the trace polyline — the governing field under POL-RD-01 — the vehicle covered 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8%. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass: 25.8% exceeds the 20% threshold and 5.78 km exceeds the 0.8 km threshold. The trip_record's rounded 28.2 km is not cited for the threshold; the trace figure is.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — quoted_fare_sgd 34.50, fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE — so POL-RD-11 governs and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. That does not leave the driver keeping the whole fare: POL-RD-11 limits the rider's remedy to the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Charged_total is 39.00; the quote is 34.50; the difference of 4.50 is made up entirely of the two ERP lines on the fare breakdown. That 4.50 is the pool the rider can recover from, and the next claims show 2.00 of it must come back.

The $2.00 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' line is a phantom charge and is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction. The gantry sits at 1.287, 103.806 and is not on the optimal route; the closest the trace ever comes to it is 5,419 m, at the very first fix of the trip. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing, and the vehicle was never within sixteen times that radius. POL-RD-09(4) makes this refundable whether or not a deviation exists, so it stands independently of the distance question.

Reconciling the fare on the record yields exactly the sum the rider is owed. The only properly chargeable gantry is the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) pass at $2.50: it lies on the booked optimal route and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it at 21:32:40, comfortably inside the 250 m match radius. The arithmetic is therefore charged_total 39.00, less the 34.50 quote, less the 2.50 KPE pass the rider did in fact incur, less waiting_time_fee 0.00 — leaving $2.00 owing to the rider, with the phantom AYE line removed.

The driver's traffic excuse cannot exonerate the detour. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING: the identifier carries no payload, weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, whose own detail records that no LTA advisory covers the CTE, the KPE or the TPE in the 21:06–21:48 window. There is accordingly no advisory to name the affected segment, no validity window to overlap the trip, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which a capped justified excess could be computed. The driver's bare 'CTE northbound was heavy' is precisely the general assertion that POL-RD-08 says does not discharge the burden of pointing to a specific artifact and clause.

The chat log does not shift the cost onto the rider. POL-RD-04 exonerates only an instruction that comes from the rider. The only message proposing the KPE–TPE route is the driver's, sent at 21:14:10; the rider's single reply, 'ok' at 21:14:50, names no road and no waypoint and its waypoint_hint is null. A message from the driver, acknowledged without any place or road being identified, is not a rider instruction, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver and the 5.78 km of excess remains unjustified.

Nothing on this record compels escalation, and a terminal escalation would only hold the disputed amount rather than return it. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 100% coverage, 229 fixes, no gaps, and a maximum consecutive-fix gap of 0 seconds against a 90-second limb (a) threshold, so limbs (a), (b) and (c) never fire. POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered by the unmatched AYE line, because that line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts and POL-RD-09(4) expressly says does not engage POL-RD-10(8). The trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match and the timestamps agree, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire either.

No extra corroboration burden attaches to the rider here. POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration condition requires deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 1 or fewer; the rider's profile shows 0 and 0. The trace alone therefore carries the excess, and the rider's threshold case is complete on limbs (a) and (b) of POL-RD-08.

This trip is an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare: the fare_breakdown carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 and null per-km and per-minute rates because there is no meter. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the rider is already whole on distance and time — so her request to 'refund the extra distance' is unavailable to her however long the route actually driven, and the driver cannot be charged for it.

On an upfront-quoted trip the rider's only monetary remedy is the amount by which charged_total (39.00) exceeds quoted_fare_sgd (34.50) plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That gap is exactly 4.50, which is precisely the two billed ERP lines (2.50 KPE + 2.00 AYE) — so there is no distance or time overcharge anywhere in this fare, and nothing beyond the pass-through lines can be owed.

The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) charge of 2.50 is properly chargeable and must not be refunded: it lies on the optimal route (on_optimal_route true) and the driver's own trace passes within 44.5 m of the gantry at 21:32:40, comfortably inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 sets for matching a gantry to the trace.

I do not contest the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of 2.00: the closest the trace ever comes to that gantry is 5,419 m and the gantry is not on the optimal route, so it is an unmatched billing line that POL-RD-09(4) refunds in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. That defect is the ledger's, not the driver's — his own trace and his own statement both put him nowhere near the AYE — so it supports a billing-integrity referral only, and the correction is capped at that single 2.00 line.

Even taking the deviation as established on the trace (excess 5.78 km, 25.8% of optimal), it is NOT a MATERIAL deviation: the material gates are 8.0 km and 50% of optimal and neither is met, so POL-RD-06's mandatory driver-profile check is not triggered by materiality. In any event the driver's 90-day record is 1 deviation flag over 523 completed trips (0.19%), nowhere near the 3-flag or 5% pattern thresholds, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists and no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral can follow from it.

Nothing in this record warrants escalation. The trace is unimpaired — 100% coverage, 229 fixes at a steady 10 s sample interval, no gaps and a 0 s maximum gap — so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire; the trip identifier TRP-00115 matches across the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown and their timestamps are consistent, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire; and the only unmatched fare line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes from escalation. The dispute should be ruled on the merits rather than held.

The driver's case does not rest on any traffic advisory, so the absent advisory EV-ADVIS-00115-01 (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE in the 21:06-21:48 window) is immaterial: no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. The driver relies on POL-RD-11, which needs no advisory at all.

No driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is warranted: no pattern is established under POL-RD-06, the deviation is not material, and the driver disclosed the reroute in the app at 21:14:10 ('CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE') which the rider acknowledged at 21:14:50 — the opposite of concealment. That exchange is not a rider instruction identifying a place or road, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to either side, but it shows the driver acted openly rather than hiding a detour.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 on EV-FARE-00115), which decides most of the case.

THE DISTANCE CLAIM. The rider is right on the facts and wrong on the money. On the governing trace figure (EV-GPS-00115, trace_distance_km 28.18, not the rounded 28.2 on the trip record) the car covered 5.78 km / 25.8% more than the 22.4 km booked optimal, so a deviation IS established under POL-RD-01 (both gates, 20% and 0.8 km, pass). It is not a MATERIAL deviation (needs 50% or 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check was not required on materiality; I ran it anyway and there is no pattern — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d 523 (0.19%), far below 3 flags or 5%. But under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges on an upfront-quoted trip were fixed at $34.50 at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the rider cannot recover for the extra distance however large the excess is. The driver's attempt to be paid for the detour also fails: POL-RD-04 needs a rider instruction naming a place or road, and the only route message is the driver's own at 21:14:10 ('CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE'), acknowledged by the rider with 'ok' and a null waypoint_hint. POL-RD-03 fails too — EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, no advisory covers CTE/KPE/TPE in the window), so there is no advisory, no validity window and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km, and a bare 'traffic was heavy' does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08.

THE MONEY. Charged total was $39.00 against the $34.50 quote — a gap of $4.50, and that gap is exactly the two ERP lines (EV-FARE-00115). One of them stands: KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) at $2.50, on the optimal route, with the trace passing within 44.5 m at 21:32:40, inside the 250 m crossing radius, so it is properly chargeable. The other does not: 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' at $2.00, not on the optimal route, and the closest the trace ever comes to that gantry is 5,419 m — sixteen times the match radius. That is a phantom billing line, refunded in full as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), which is available whether or not a deviation exists. Refund = charged_total 39.00 − quoted_fare 34.50 − properly chargeable KPE pass 2.50 − waiting_time_fee 0.00 = $2.00. The rider's own reconciliation reaches the same $2.00.

NO ESCALATION AND NO CONDUCT REFERRAL. The trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 229 fixes, 10 s interval, maximum gap 0 s), so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) do not fire; trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the artifacts, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire; and the only unmatched fare line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review is not engaged because no repeat pattern exists and the deviation is not material. All of these artifacts carry weight 1.0, so nothing is discounted and nothing is held.

RESULT. PARTIAL_REFUND of $2.00 to the rider; the rest of the charge stands. A billing-integrity referral on the phantom AYE line is recorded above.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: review the fare ledger for the phantom gantry line 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' of $2.00, charged on trip TRP-00115 although the GPS trace never came within 5,419 m of that gantry (match radius 250 m) and the gantry is not on the optimal route; the line is refunded in full and the ledger entry is flagged.
